scenes.text:
Quill moves his bowl aside. "Replay. Mara Voss, Helion logistics. Glass Chapel edits her memory at dawn. Bring me the original hour, intact. Fifty now, two hundred on delivery. Her bodyguard is Kerr. He is paid to stop you."

You came for enough money to keep tomorrow yours. You want the terms before the promises. Somewhere above the rain, a file with your old name is still open.

The stallholder’s story stays with you. Whose hour are you being asked to carry? Quill has not touched his dinner. You have not agreed to the job.

Quill turns the untouched bowl away from the edge. "Do not give me an easy yes. I need you to come back with the hour."

Ninety is already on your chip. Try not to donate it to a door. You tell Quill you need tomorrow paid for. "Then do not spend your whole advance on my pass," he says. "There are other doors."

"Three ways in. The front sells forgiveness to anyone with an appointment. The hatch behind the incinerator is for people who still sweat. The choir door runs on an old Helion pad. I would not kiss it."

The penitent pass is a hundred. It scans often enough. Glass Chapel is three streets over. You leave the steam of the stall for its white light.

Edda smooths the request form once. Her hand stops above the signature line.

"A fee, an old number, a signature. Each leaves someone carrying this request. I want to know which part you are asking me to carry."

She can help carry this bounded record. The families stay out of the request.

A staffed movement-page extraction costs twenty-five creds and logs a query. A Spire employee can bill it to the old badge, adding its trace. Earned Face training lets you ask Edda for a bounded countersignature instead: she agrees to this extraction, and her employer can identify her signed shift. None of these methods tests an issuing key.

"The tea will be cold. Sit down anyway."

Her cup leaves a pale ring on the table. The rain goes on.
